comment_00_what: 🏛️ RECOMMENDED RoC CONFIG (Frontend/Angular) — generated by RuleOfCode {{ROC_VERSION}} for {{PROJECT_NAME}} on {{GENERATED_AT}}. This file is a REFERENCE, not the active config: RoC does not read it automatically. Use it with `npx ruleofcode audit --config ROC-RECOMMENDED.ruleofcode.config.json`, or carry its decisions over into your own ruleofcode.config.json. It is regenerated on every RoC upgrade.
comment_01_principle: PRINCIPLE: a silently disarmed gate is more dangerous than a missing gate. Three rules this config enforces: (1) NO includes whitelist — real case: an Nx workspace lost an entire library (54 files, 26% of the code) from the audit because no one had added it to the whitelist; the audit stayed green. (2) notApplicable means 'this concern DOES NOT EXIST here' — NOT 'we haven't gotten to it yet'. Debt is shown as a warning, not hidden as a waiver. (3) Every waiver carries a reason; if it is temporary — it also carries a DATE and an OWNER.
comment_02_includes: ❌ NO includes.global — DELIBERATELY. A positive whitelist requires someone to remember to add every new library; when they forget, the code passes the audit because no one looked at it. Without a whitelist, a new library is covered from the day it is created.
comment_03_ignores: Generated artifacts only. Test files are NOT listed — RoC excludes them from the code laws by default. Do NOT put environment.ts/secret files in global ignores (that hides them from ALL laws) — exclude them surgically from the specific law via ignores.byRule using its slug (`roc laws --list`).
comment_04_laws: THREE LEVELS, clearly separated: error = the line that is not crossed · warning = REAL DEBT, made VISIBLE (not waived) · notApplicable = the concern does not exist. failOnWarnings: true is the strongest safeguard — every warning fails the audit, INCLUDING laws that future versions of RoC add as warnings. If you are not yet at zero warnings, leave it false and burn down the debt via the ladder (comment_06).
comment_05_minLaws: minLawsChecked (law 226 Audit Liveness): the audit FAILS if it runs fewer laws than this threshold. Born from a real incident — RoC v7.5.1 ran ZERO laws and printed PASSED with exit 0. The value above is ~90% of those applicable to this stack today; raise it to your real post-waiver count once you know it (see `Total Laws Checked` in the output).
comment_06_ladder: 🪜 LADDER (warn→fix→error): run the audit once, record which laws light up as warnings and with how many violations. Burn them down one by one; once a law reaches 0, raise it to error in laws.severity — so it cannot come back. When ALL reach 0 → failOnWarnings: true. Typical candidates for early escalation (usually already clean): no-passthrough-cast · defensive-array-coercion · timer-cleanup · stores-in-data-access · no-hostname-gating · poll-via-sanctioned-source.
comment_07_file_size: File length is enforced by Code Complexity Control (law 14) via thresholds.codeQuality.maxFileLines (default 300 — the same threshold as for Python). The law is a warning by default: raise it to error in laws.severity once the long files are split. Do NOT raise the threshold to pass — that hides exactly the debt that needs to be seen.
comment_08_golden: goldenPaths (law 232 Golden Fixture Immutability): declare your jest snapshot/golden files and any change to them will require an entry in GOLDEN-APPROVALS.md in the SAME change-set. A silent snapshot regeneration masks a regression — the code approves its own new behavior. Leave empty if you have no snapshot tests.
comment_09_cache: cache: false — a cached compliance result may report a stale PASSED. The audit is a gate, not a build step.
comment_04b_process_laws: ⚙️ PROCESS/ARTIFACT laws (lowered to warning in laws.severity): they look for ARTIFACTS — checklists, CI configs, incident docs, PR/commit conventions, MD footers — not properties of the code. That is why they are VISIBLE (warning) but do not block the gate. Decide for each: if the concern REALLY lives outside the repo (DevOps/org layer) → move it to notApplicable with a reason. If it does not live outside → burn it down and raise it to error. Do not leave them on warning forever — that is a waiting room, not a destination.
comment_04c_domain_laws: 🏗️ DOMAIN/INFRA laws (lowered to warning): they check concerns that may not exist at all in this project (SQL queries, APM, CDN, health endpoint, RBAC). Decide for each: there is NO such concern (e.g. you have no SQL DB) → notApplicable with a reason. It DOES exist → burn it down and raise it to error. Left on warning so they do not block the gate before you have decided — but stay visible.
comment_04d_stack_policy: 🖼️ FRONTEND POLICY laws (lowered to warning): bundle/CWV/lazy-loading/i18n depend on the build tool and the product decision (e.g. esbuild does chunking automatically; CWV is measured with Lighthouse; a single-language product). Code Documentation / Unit Test Quality / E2E are REAL DEBT — visible, not hidden. Same rule: no concern → notApplicable with a reason; it exists → burn it down.
